Definition: from G712; to take the principle meal:--dine.
BiblicalUsage: To dine is to take the main meal of the day, and the Gospels use it for ordinary meals and one extraordinary one. A Pharisee invites Jesus to dine with him, and after the resurrection Jesus stands on the shore and calls the disciples to come and dine, fish and bread already waiting.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the risen Jesus cooking breakfast says something no sermon could: He is not a ghost or an idea, He is the Lord who feeds His friends. The table is where He meets them, and I hold that He still meets us there, in the ordinary act of eating together.
